terms.meaning: The tree of categories that describes an industry, from broad groups down to specific items.
The menu a user picks a segment from.
A category at the bottom of a tree that has no children.
A group in an industry's tree used for choosing and filtering.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: How chooser levels are picked
sections.what: The header comment says a segment is a chooser-level node in an industry's tree, and that the level depends on the industry's structure. It also says whether a chooser appears is set by a separate flag, not by counting items.
sections.why: The comment explains that counting items alone gave wrong answers for nuclear and mining, which both have one non-empty segment.
sections.watch_out: Do not infer whether a chooser shows from item counts, because the explicit flag controls it.

sections.name: SegmentNode
sections.title: Shape of one segment
sections.what: Describes one selectable segment in an industry's chooser: its name, plus the group heading it sits under if it has one.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the chooser show segments under group headings.

sections.name: getSegmentNodes
sections.title: Turning an industry into segments
sections.what: Builds the list of segments shown for one industry. Value-chain industries get one segment per top-level step. Other industries get the children of a group as segments under that group's heading when the group has sub-items, and otherwise the top-level item becomes its own segment. Unknown industries get an empty list.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The group-heading test only looks two levels down, so deeper nesting may not be grouped the way the owner expects.

sections.name: collectNames
sections.title: Gathering a name and everything below it
sections.what: Collects a node's name together with the names of all items nested under it, at any depth, into one flat list.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code; it is a helper used when a segment is expanded.

sections.name: findNode
sections.title: Finding a node by name
sections.what: Searches the whole industry tree, at any depth, for the first node with a matching name and returns it, or nothing if none matches.
sections.why: Likely reason: a segment name from the web address can sit at any level, so the search checks every level.
sections.watch_out: If two nodes in different branches share a name, only the first one found is used.

sections.name: expandSegment
sections.title: Expanding a segment to include its sub-items
sections.what: Given an industry and a segment name, returns that segment's name plus all names beneath it. The app uses this list to match projects, so choosing a parent segment also includes its sub-segments. Returns an empty list if the segment is not in the tree.
sections.why: Likely reason: a project tagged with a sub-item should still count under its parent segment, as the comment states.
sections.watch_out: The duplicate-name issue from the search helper applies here too, so the wrong branch may be chosen.

sections.name: hasSegmentChooser
sections.title: Checking whether the chooser is turned on
sections.what: Answers yes or no to whether an industry shows the segment chooser, based on an explicit on or off setting in that industry's configuration.
sections.why: Stated in the code comment: the chooser is switched on by an explicit setting, not by default.
sections.watch_out: How an unknown industry is handled depends on getIndustryConfig, which is not in this file.

why: The header comment says the chooser level depends on the industry's structure, and that a separate flag decides whether a chooser appears at all.
how: Based only on the header: for value-chain industries the chooser is the first stage level, and for sub-industry industries it is the first or second level depending on whether the children have their own children. The remaining functions were not visible, so their steps are unknown.
inputs: An industry name and its taxonomy tree, as implied by the imports. Not verified beyond the import lines.
outputs: Not visible in the provided section.
risks: Changing the shape of a taxonomy can silently change which level is the chooser. Whether a chooser appears is controlled by a flag, not by counts.
